CVE-2026-111872.description: A security vulnerability has been detected in itsmeravitejak Online-Examination-System up to e6208e630b14657999bbfe4c9912302d2a1e2449. This affects the function MySQLDB::valid/MySQLDB::getresults/MySQLDB::noresults/MySQLDB::getExams/MySQLDB::latestExamID/MySQLDB::getreport of the file results.php/include/database.php. The manipulation of the argument id/user/topic leads to sql injection. The attack may be initiated remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. This product uses a rolling release model to deliver continuous updates. As a result, specific version information for affected or updated releases is not available. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-111873.description: A vulnerability was detected in itsmeravitejak Online-Examination-System up to e6208e630b14657999bbfe4c9912302d2a1e2449. This impacts the function MySQLDB::topicslist of the file exammanger.php of the component AJAX Endpoint. The manipulation of the argument subject results in sql injection. The attack may be launched remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. This product operates on a rolling release basis, ensuring continuous delivery. Consequently, there are no version details for either affected or updated releases. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-111874.description: A flaw has been found in OpenCATS 0.10.0. Affected is the function processLogin of the file modules/careers/CareersUI.php of the component Career Portal. This manipulation of the argument applyToJobSubAction causes improper restriction of excessive authentication attempts. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. A high degree of complexity is needed for the attack. The exploitability is told to be difficult. The exploit has been published and may be used. Patch name: 1cf4fa3ee9054314b023be79d404078645c22ade. It is suggested to install a patch to address this issue. The project maintainer explains: "Candidates will now need to authenticate each time they access the Career Portal and successfully complete the CAPTCHA as part of that authentication flow. The authenticated candidate identity is now maintained server-side rather than relying on the previous persistent client-side cats…cw cookie mechanism. Application-level rate limiting is deliberately not in scope for this change. In my view, request throttling and brute-force protection of that kind are better applied at the network, reverse-proxy or web-server layer, where they can be configured appropriately for each deployment without OpenCATS having to implement and maintain its own rate-limiting framework. I'll update the online documentation to that effect."

CVE-2026-111875.description: A vulnerability has been found in David-Crty Databasement up to 1.8.1. Affected by this vulnerability is an unknown functionality of the file app/Http/Requests/Api/V1/SaveScheduledRestoreRequest.php of the component Scheduled Restore. Such manipulation of the argument schema_name leads to missing authorization. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.8.2 addresses this issue. It is suggested to upgrade the affected component.

CVE-2026-111876.description: A vulnerability was found in alexpasmantier television up to 0.15.9. Affected by this issue is the function Entry::output of the file television/channels/entry.rs. Performing a manipulation of the argument raw results in command injection. The attack requires a local approach. The reported GitHub issue was closed with the label "not planned".

CVE-2026-109937.description: The Otter Blocks WordPress plugin before 3.2.3 does not validate that a user-supplied return URL belongs to the site before using it to build the return destination of a Stripe Checkout session, allowing unauthenticated attackers to redirect victims who complete or cancel checkout to an arbitrary external URL.

CVE-2026-110026.description: The Tasty Recipes Lite WordPress plugin before 1.2.11 does not correctly check user capabilities when creating, renaming and deleting taxonomy terms, allowing users with a role as low as Contributor to add, rename and permanently delete terms in any taxonomy on the site, including categories, tags and navigation menus.

CVE-2026-110031.description: The Salon Booking System WordPress plugin before 10.31.11 does not prevent users holding its custom salon staff role from assigning arbitrary capabilities to other accounts when editing a customer, allowing them to escalate any account to administrator and take over the site.

CVE-2026-110032.description: The Salon Booking System WordPress plugin before 10.31.11 does not restrict which user account its salon staff roles may edit through the customers management screen, allowing users with the Salon Staff or Salon Worker role to reset any other user's role, including administrators, to a customer and to overwrite arbitrary profile fields on any account, leading to loss of administrative access and potential site lockout.

CVE-2026-110033.description: The Salon Booking System WordPress plugin before 10.31.11 does not validate a user-supplied image URL before fetching it server-side and writing the response to a publicly accessible location under an attacker-chosen filename, allowing users with the Salon Staff role or higher to force the server to read internal-only resources and disclose them, and to store a malicious SVG that runs arbitrary scripts in the site's origin for anyone who opens it.

CVE-2026-110035.description: The Salon Booking System WordPress plugin before 10.31.11 does not restrict one of its REST API endpoints to salon staff, allowing any authenticated user, such as a subscriber, to retrieve every discount coupon configured on the site, including coupons the administrator has chosen to hide from customers, together with their amounts, validity dates and usage limits.

CVE-2026-110069.description: The Modern Events Calendar Lite WordPress plugin before 7.37.0 does not perform capability, nonce, or ownership checks before returning event booking and attendee data, allowing any authenticated user, including Subscribers, to disclose the names, email addresses, transaction IDs and payment amounts of every booking on the site.

CVE-2026-110070.description: The Modern Events Calendar Lite WordPress plugin before 7.36.4 does not verify that a user is authorized to edit the target post before updating it, allowing authenticated users with the Subscriber role to modify the title, content, and excerpt of arbitrary posts, pages, and custom post types created by other users.

CVE-2026-110976.description: The AI Engine WordPress plugin before 3.7.9 does not check that the item passed to one of its media actions belongs to the requesting user before converting it to an attachment and permanently deleting it, allowing users with the Editor role and above to delete arbitrary posts of any type, including content they cannot otherwise delete such as navigation menus, block templates and global styles.

CVE-2026-110981.description: The WP Photo Album Plus WordPress plugin before 9.2.11.002 does not properly escape a category navigation value before reflecting it into a JavaScript event handler on its gallery breadcrumb links, allowing unauthenticated attackers to inject arbitrary script that executes in the browser of anyone who follows a crafted gallery link and clicks the breadcrumb, including a logged-in administrator.

CVE-2026-111041.description: The AI Engine WordPress plugin before 3.7.9 does not verify that the user performing certain AI media management actions owns or is otherwise allowed to edit the targeted object, allowing users with the Editor role or above to modify, or change the type of, arbitrary posts on the site, including content they are not permitted to edit.

CVE-2026-111877.description: A vulnerability was determined in dext34-morgan Books4Cash up to a8d3e357db75c07ac5ffbadcbaee2aeb4db3e571. This affects an unknown part of the file search.php. Executing a manipulation of the argument Search can lead to cross site scripting. The attack may be performed from remote. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The code repository of the project has not been active for many years.

CVE-2026-111942.description: A weakness has been identified in hrisikeshpal Blood_Bank_Management_System 1.0.0. Impacted is an unknown function of the file /abs.php. This manipulation of the argument Search causes cross site scripting. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-87844.description: The PickPlugins Product Designer for WooCommerce WordPress plugin through 1.0.40 does not perform any capability check and its nonce verification is inverted, accepting requests with an invalid or absent nonce while rejecting valid ones, and it does not validate the post the data is written to, allowing unauthenticated users to insert design template data into the metadata of any post on the site.

CVE-2026-96534.description: The Modern Events Calendar Lite WordPress plugin before 7.37.0, Modern Event Calendar Pro WordPress plugin before 7.37.0 does not sanitise and escape a parameter before using it in a SQL statement, allowing authenticated users with minimal privileges (Subscriber and above) to perform SQL injection attacks.

CVE-2026-107436.description: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in WP Chill Strong Testimonials strong-testimonials allows Object Injection.This issue affects Strong Testimonials: from n/a through 3.3.12.

CVE-2026-108485.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in ThemeGrill eStore estore allows Reflected XSS.This issue affects eStore: from n/a through 1.6.13.

CVE-2026-109894.description: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in Arraytics Booktics booktics allows SQL Injection.This issue affects Booktics: from n/a through 1.0.29.

CVE-2026-109895.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Arraytics Booktics booktics allows DOM-Based XSS.This issue affects Booktics: from n/a through 1.0.29.

CVE-2026-110365.description: Missing Authorization vulnerability in WPExperts Advanced File Manager file-manager-advanced allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Advanced File Manager: from n/a through 5.4.14.

CVE-2026-110372.description: Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in Brainstorm Force OttoKit suretriggers allows Privilege Escalation.This issue affects OttoKit: from n/a through 1.1.40.

CVE-2026-110373.description: Incorrect Privilege Assignment vulnerability in Hamid Alinia Login with phone number login-with-phone-number allows Privilege Escalation.This issue affects Login with phone number: from n/a through 1.8.77.

CVE-2026-110382.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in NSquared Simply Schedule Appointments simply-schedule-appointments allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Simply Schedule Appointments: from n/a through 1.6.12.35.

CVE-2026-110383.description: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key vulnerability in WP E-Signature Electronic Signature Add-on for Fluent Forms signature-fluent-contract-forms-add-on allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Electronic Signature Add-on for Fluent Forms: from n/a through 2.0.5.

CVE-2026-110880.description: Missing Authorization vulnerability in Kit Kit (formerly ConvertKit) convertkit allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Kit (formerly ConvertKit): from n/a through 3.4.6.

CVE-2026-110883.description: Authentication Bypass by Primary Weakness vulnerability in VideoWhisper.com 2Way VideoCalls and Random Chat webcam-2way-videochat allows Authentication Abuse.This issue affects 2Way VideoCalls and Random Chat: from n/a through 6.1.5.

CVE-2026-110885.description: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection') vulnerability in HivePress HivePress hivepress allows Code Injection.This issue affects HivePress: from n/a through 1.7.32.

CVE-2026-110886.description: Deserialization of Untrusted Data vulnerability in QuantumCloud Conversational Forms for ChatBot conversational-forms allows Object Injection.This issue affects Conversational Forms for ChatBot: from n/a through 1.5.1.

CVE-2026-110895.description: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in DevItems Support Genix support-genix-lite allows SQL Injection.This issue affects Support Genix: from n/a through 1.4.54.

CVE-2026-110897.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in IdeaBox Creations PowerPack Lite for Beaver Builder powerpack-addon-for-beaver-builder allows Stored XSS.This issue affects PowerPack Lite for Beaver Builder: from n/a through 1.3.1.

CVE-2026-111984.description: A vulnerability has been found in AUTOMATIC1111 stable-diffusion-webui up to 1.10.1. This affects the function create_item_html of the file modules/ui_extra_networks.py of the component Card Builder. The manipulation of the argument filename leads to cross site scripting. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-111985.description: A vulnerability was found in AUTOMATIC1111 stable-diffusion-webui up to 1.10.1. This impacts the function read_metadata_from_safetensors of the file modules/sd_models.py of the component Metadata Extraction. The manipulation of the argument header length field results in allocation of resources. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been made public and could be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-111998.description: Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a default credentials vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to gain cluster-admin access by using the hardcoded admin token. Attackers can send the fixed Bearer token to the gateway gRPC proxy port to manage namespaces, eventbuses, users, tokens, and role bindings, and read or publish events.

CVE-2026-111999.description: Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to publish events to any eventbus through the gateway CloudEvents HTTP receiver. Attackers can send forged CloudEvents to the /namespaces/{ns}/eventbus/{name}/events or legacy /gateway/{name} paths, bypassing token authentication and authPublish checks, so they are stored and delivered to subscription sinks.

CVE-2026-112000.description: Vanus 0.8.0 through 0.9.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the gateway that allows any authenticated user to call Subscribe, Ack, and unregistered methods without permission checks. Attackers can supply another tenant's subscription ID to Subscribe to hijack it, read and acknowledge its events, starve the legitimate consumer, and enumerate cluster users via ListUser.

CVE-2026-112001.description: ProjectSend 2.0.0 before 2.7.0 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows restricted API token holders to change the token owner's credentials via PATCH /api/v1/users/{user}. Attackers with a token limited to manage_users and edit_users can set a new owner password, clear two-factor authentication, and sign in interactively with the owner's full role permissions.

CVE-2026-112002.description: ProjectSend 2.5.0 before 2.7.0 contains an unverified password change vulnerability in PasswordController::update() that lets sessions of Social-provisioned accounts set local passwords without the current password. Attackers holding a stolen session cookie can send PUT /settings/password to create a durable local password, enroll their own second factor, and persistently take over the account.

CVE-2026-112003.description: ProjectSend 2.0.0 before 2.7.0 contains a path validation flaw in OrphanFileScanner::isOrphan() that allows staff with import_orphans permission to treat tracked files as orphans. Attackers can submit ./ path aliases to the orphans import or delete endpoints, deleting or adopting other owners' files while bypassing delete_others_files.

CVE-2026-112004.description: Teable before 2026-10-12T12-45-53Z.3331 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows authenticated users to rename folders in other bases by supplying a foreign folderId. The PATCH /api/base/:baseId/node/folder/:folderId endpoint checks base|update only against the URL baseId, so attackers can rename folders in bases where they lack membership.

CVE-2026-112005.description: WhoDB 0.104.0 before 0.135.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows remote attackers to read and write arbitrary host files by running DuckDB filesystem functions through the query editor. Attackers can log in to a DuckDB file without credentials and use read_text, read_blob, COPY ... TO or ATTACH to steal session.key and stored database credentials or overwrite files.

CVE-2026-112006.description: OpenTelemetry opentelemetry-exporter-otlp-proto-http 1.5.0 before 1.45.0 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability that disables TLS verification when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_CERTIFICATE variables are empty strings. Man-in-the-middle attackers can impersonate the collector to read or alter exported traces, metrics, and logs, including authentication headers from OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS.

CVE-2026-112007.description: Schism Tracker through 20260524 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in fmt_ult_load_song() in fmt/ult.c that fails to clamp the one-byte sample count to MAX_SAMPLES. Attackers can supply a crafted .ult module that overwrites the instruments pointer array, causing csf_destroy() to free attacker-chosen pointers and crash the application.

CVE-2026-112008.description: libmng through 2.0.3 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in mng_read_ordr() that allows attackers to corrupt heap memory because ORDR entry buffers are sized by 5-byte on-wire records instead of 8-byte in-memory entries. Attackers can supply a crafted MNG file with MHDR, DHDR and a multi-record ORDR chunk to applications calling mng_read or mng_readdisplay, writing attacker-controlled data past the allocation and crashing the application.

CVE-2026-112009.description: smpeg through 2.0.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in MPEGsystem::FillBuffer() that allows attackers to read past the 16384-byte buffer by supplying a crafted system header stream table. Attackers can provide an MPEG file whose stream table bytes all set the high bit, which crashes applications opening it through SMPEG_new, SMPEG_new_rwops, or SMPEG_new_data.

CVE-2026-112010.description: smpeg through 2.0.0 contains an integer underflow vulnerability in stream_header() in MPEGsystem.cpp that allows attackers to wrap packet_size by declaring an undersized packet length. Attackers can supply a crafted MPEG file opened via SMPEG_new, SMPEG_new_rwops or SMPEG_new_data to trigger a reachable assertion or out-of-bounds copy, crashing the application.

CVE-2026-112011.description: libtta through 2.3 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in tta_decoder_init_get_info() that allows attackers to cause a heap buffer overflow on 32-bit builds via unvalidated header fields. Attackers can supply a crafted .tta file with a sample rate of 1 and large samples value, wrapping the seek table allocation and crashing applications.

CVE-2026-112012.description: libtta through 2.3 contains a stack out-of-bounds read and write vulnerability in tta_decoder_process_stream() and tta_decoder_process_frame() because header checks never reject a zero channel count. Attackers can supply a crafted .tta file declaring zero channels so decorrelation accesses cache[-1] with stream-derived values, corrupting stack memory in decoding applications.

CVE-2026-112013.description: libtta through 2.3 contains a divide-by-zero vulnerability in tta_decoder_init_get_info() that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying an unvalidated zero sample rate. Attackers can craft a .tta file with a recomputed header CRC32 that triggers SIGFPE, crashing applications including the bundled tta console tool.

CVE-2026-112014.description: LobsterAI before 2026.10.16 contains a hardcoded password vulnerability that allows attackers to decrypt exported provider API keys encrypted with the constant 'lobsterai-APP'. Attackers who obtain a providers export file can derive the AES-GCM key via PBKDF2 using the embedded salt and recover every third-party AI provider API key.

CVE-2026-112015.description: Omnigent 0.3.0 before 0.14.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to escape the workspace by setting os_env.cwd on nested sub-agents. Attackers can upload a bundle whose sub-agent uses an absolute or parent-traversing working directory, bypassing root-only validation in bundles.py, to read and write host files as the runner user.

CVE-2026-112016.description: Netcore NR256CN through 1.5.140116 contains an unauthenticated file write vulnerability in the Boa-derived /bin/boa web server that allows remote attackers to overwrite update and restore staging files. Attackers can POST to a non-existent .cgi pathname to write attacker-controlled content into /tmp/boa_temp.update or /tmp/boa_temp.para, tampering with pending firmware updates or configuration restores or causing denial of service.

CVE-2026-112017.description: JeecgBoot before 3.9.5 contains an sql injection vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to bypass the SqlInjectionUtil keyword blocklist by inserting newline characters into dictionary and online report SQL fragments. Attackers can send newline-separated payloads to endpoints like /sys/dict/getDictItems for boolean or time-based blind injection, extracting database contents including administrator password hashes from sys_user.

CVE-2026-112018.description: cgltf through 1.15 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in cgltf_accessor_unpack_floats() that allows attackers to write outside the output buffer via unchecked sparse accessor indices. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF or GLB file with large sparse indices to corrupt heap memory, crash applications, and potentially execute code when cgltf_validate() is not called.

CVE-2026-112019.description: cgltf through 1.15 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in cgltf_accessor_unpack_floats() that advances the sparse values cursor by the base bufferView byteStride. Attackers can supply a crafted glTF or GLB file that passes cgltf_validate() to read adjacent heap memory into vertex data or crash applications.

CVE-2026-112020.description: LodePNG through 20261006 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in lodepng::getFilterTypesInterlaced() in lodepng_util.cpp that lacks bounds checks on decompressed IDAT data. Attackers can supply a crafted interlaced PNG declaring a raster larger than its IDAT stream to disclose adjacent heap memory or crash applications.

CVE-2026-112021.description: snac2 before 2.93 contains a heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in _xs_json_load_lexer() that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to corrupt heap memory by sending JSON strings containing a \u0000 escape. Attackers can send a single crafted application/activity+json POST to activitypub_post_handler(), which parses it before signature checks, overflowing heap allocations and crashing the server.

CVE-2026-78497.description: JQ::Lite versions before 2.51 for Perl execute Perl code embedded in a query's regular expression by compiling it with string eval. The pattern given to test(), match(), or the match and =~ conditions of select() is placed in a `qr'...'` literal and compiled as source text, so a `(?{ ... })` code block in it runs without `use re 'eval'`. Single quotes in the pattern are escaped, but a code block runs in place and needs none. An attacker who supplies a query, or text that an application inserts into the pattern of one, can execute arbitrary Perl code in the calling process.

CVE-2026-111986.description: A vulnerability was determined in AUTOMATIC1111 stable-diffusion-webui up to 1.10.1. Affected is the function get_obj_from_str of the file modules/sd_models.py of the component Model Instantiation. This manipulation of the argument Target causes code injection. The attack can be initiated remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

CVE-2026-112046.description: OW2 ASM 9.11 before 9.11.1 contains an infinite loop vulnerability in Label.resolve() caused by 16-bit forward-reference offsets truncating when rewritten methods exceed 64 KB. Attackers can supply crafted class files whose transformed code grows past 65535 bytes, hanging ClassReader.accept() and denying service to build tools, instrumenters, agents, or analyzers.

CVE-2026-112047.description: OneUptime 14.0.2 before 14.0.69 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated project members to act on clusters outside their scope by exploiting project-wide permission checks. Attackers can call the AI access test, agent reset, kubectl plan approval and incident AI conversation features to learn agent RBAC permissions, disconnect agents, approve kubectl changes, or run commands on unauthorized resources.

CVE-2026-112048.description: libspatialite through 5.1.0 fails to validate the polygon ring count in ParseWkbPolygon, allowing attackers to trigger uncontrolled interior-ring allocation via crafted geometry BLOBs. Attackers can supply a crafted polygon in a SpatiaLite database or ST_GeomFromWKB input to crash the process or corrupt heap memory on 32-bit builds.

CVE-2026-112049.description: Vita3K before build 4187 contains a path traversal (zip slip) vulnerability in install_archive_content() that allows attackers to write files outside the install directory via crafted .vpk archives. Attackers can embed '..' segments or absolute paths in zip entry names to write attacker-controlled files anywhere writable by Vita3K, potentially enabling host code execution.

CVE-2026-112050.description: Gitify before 7.10.0 contains a login cross-site request forgery vulnerability that allows remote attackers to bind a victim's client to their account because performGitHubWebOAuth() omits OAuth state validation. Attackers can get a gitify://oauth?code= link with their own authorization code opened during a victim's pending login, causing Gitify to display attacker-controlled notifications as the victim's own.

CVE-2026-112051.description: Xinference through 4.0.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability on Windows that allows unauthenticated attackers to write and delete arbitrary .json files via backslash sequences in model_name. Attackers can register a persisted custom model through POST /v1/model_registrations/{model_type} with names like ..\..\evil to overwrite configuration or data files writable by the Xinference process.

CVE-2026-112052.description: libspatialite through 5.1.0 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in the WKB point and vertex count size guard of ParseWkbLine and related parsers in gg_wkb.c, allowing out-of-bounds reads. Attackers can supply a crafted geometry BLOB with a large point count, for example in a SpatiaLite database file, to crash the process or corrupt heap memory on 32-bit builds.

CVE-2026-112053.description: Schroedinger libschroedinger through 1.0.11 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability that allows attackers to read past a static quantiser table by supplying unvalidated wavelet filter index or transform depth values. Attackers can deliver a crafted low-delay Dirac stream with a wavelet filter index of 7 or more or transform depth of 5 or 6 to crash decoding applications.

CVE-2026-112054.description: Schroedinger libschroedinger through 1.0.11 contains a divide by zero vulnerability that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying a zero slice_bytes_denom or slice count in a Dirac stream. Attackers can provide a crafted low-delay picture parsed by schro_decoder_parse_transform_parameters and schro_decoder_parse_lowdelay_transform_data to trigger a SIGFPE and cause denial of service.

CVE-2026-112055.description: wvWare wv through 1.2.9 contains a stack-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in wvGetPAPX_FKP and wvGetCHPX_FKP caused by an unvalidated FKP run count. Attackers can supply a crafted .doc file with a large crun value to read kilobytes past the 512-byte stack buffer, crashing applications like AbiWord.

CVE-2026-112056.description: wvWare wv through 1.2.9 contains a heap-based out-of-bounds read vulnerability in wvGetSTSH in stylesheet.c that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying crafted Word stylesheets. Attackers can provide a .doc file with ten or fewer styles or out-of-range style base indexes to read past heap arrays, crashing applications such as AbiWord.

CVE-2026-112057.description: libdvdnav before 7.0.0 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in dvdnav_describe_title_chapters that allows attackers to read beyond the part-of-title array by supplying an oversized vts_ttn value. Attackers can provide a crafted DVD or disc image declaring a larger VMGI title vts_ttn than the title set's entries to crash applications enumerating chapters.

CVE-2026-112058.description: VideoLAN libdvdnav through 7.0.0 contains an out-of-bounds read vulnerability in set_PTT that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying an invalid JumpTT title number checked only by an assert. Attackers can craft a DVD or disc image whose First Play program chain issues JumpTT with title 0 or an oversized number, reading past the heap title table and crashing the player.

CVE-2026-112059.description: libLAS through 1.8.1 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the point record reader caused by truncating the schema byte size to 16 bits when sizing the point buffer. Attackers can craft a .las file with a LASSchema variable length record whose schema exceeds 65535 bytes, so tools like lasinfo, las2las, or las2txt write attacker-controlled bytes past the heap buffer, causing memory corruption and crashes.

CVE-2026-112060.description: librtmp in RTMPDump through 2.6 contains an out-of-bounds read and heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability because AMF3_Decode ignores AMF3 property decode failures. Malicious RTMP servers or man-in-the-middle attackers can send oversized AMF3 string lengths, and with the token option DecodeTEA corrupts heap memory and leaks heap bytes.

CVE-2026-112061.description: librtmp (RTMPDump) through 2.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in AMFProp_Decode that reads an AMF0 strict-array element count before checking that four bytes remain. A malicious RTMP server or man in the middle can send an AMF0 body ending with a strict-array type byte and fewer than four trailing bytes to crash the client.

CVE-2026-112062.description: lwIP through 2.2.1 contains a stack out-of-bounds write vulnerability in mdns_handle_response that allows adjacent attackers to corrupt stack memory by sending mDNS responses with invalid domain names. Attackers on the local link can send multicast PTR answers with oversized RDLENGTH or SRV answers with RDLENGTH below 6 during a service search, overflowing a 256-byte stack buffer and crashing the device.

CVE-2026-112063.description: libstrophe through 0.14.0 contains a stack-based buffer overflow vulnerability in SCRAM_Hi that allows malicious XMPP servers to overflow a 128-byte stack buffer by sending an oversized SCRAM salt. Attackers can send a server-first-message whose s= attribute decodes to more than 124 bytes, aborting the client or overwriting stack memory in NDEBUG builds.

CVE-2026-111987.description: A vulnerability was identified in AUTOMATIC1111 stable-diffusion-webui up to 1.10.1. Affected by this vulnerability is the function read_metadata_from_safetensors of the file modules/sd_models.py of the component Extra-Networks Card Builder. Such manipulation of the argument __metadata__.sshs_model_hash leads to cross site scripting. The attack can be launched remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used. The project was informed of the problem early through an issue report but has not responded yet.

8e69cb52f70914a28a08638d.title_ko: 오픈AI, ‘GPT-6 아스트라 프로’에 여러 에이전트 병렬 실행 기능 추가
8e69cb52f70914a28a08638d.summary_ko: 오픈AI가 챗GPT의 ‘GPT-6 아스트라 프로’에 여러 AI 에이전트가 하나의 작업을 나눠 동시에 처리하는 병렬 실행 기능을 업데이트했다. 사용자는 대화 화면에서 각 에이전트의 진행 상황과 결과를 직접 확인하며 복잡한 작업을 효율적으로 수행할 수 있다. 이번 기능은 현재 프로 요금제 사용자들을 대상으로 제공된다.

9206c9822872744d92cd2652.title_ko: Linux 커널의 VM 탈출 취약점 'PwnEscape'(CVE-2026-99999) 발견
9206c9822872744d92cd2652.summary_ko: Vercel 주최 해킹 챌린지에서 Linux 커널의 IPv4 네트워크 처리 과정 중 발견된 치명적인 취약점 'PwnEscape'가 CVE-2026-99999로 등록되었다. 해당 취약점으로 인해 가상머신(VM) 탈출이 가능해져 VPS 사업자들의 긴급 대응이 요구되고 있다.

curation.reason_ko: Linux 커널의 VM 탈출이 가능한 고위험 취약점이 발견되어 VPS 사업자들이 긴급 대응에 나섰습니다.

51d38c216186047649ec223d.title_ko: ConnectWise, M365 테넌트 손상 사건 여파로 클라우드 백업 중단
51d38c216186047649ec223d.summary_ko: ConnectWise가 애플리케이션 식별자가 공격자에게 무단 노출되어 마이크로소프트 365 테넌트가 손상되는 보안 사고가 발생함에 따라 관련 클라우드 백업 및 관리 서비스를 일시 중단했다. 회사는 침해 여부를 조사하고 영향받은 인증 정보를 폐기하는 등 대응에 나섰다.

6adb4b6ae055053511fd51f2.title_ko: 리퀴드 AI, 성능 앞선 멀티모달 의사결정 모델 ‘d1-울트라’ 공개
6adb4b6ae055053511fd51f2.summary_ko: 리퀴드 AI가 텍스트와 이미지 분석 능력을 강화하고 판단 정확도와 확률 보정 성능을 높인 멀티모달 의사결정 모델 'd1-울트라'를 공개했다. 이 모델은 독립 평가인 아티피셜 애널리시스의 의사결정 지수에서 1위를 기록하며 기존 경쟁 모델들을 앞섰다.

ee85afdfd4a43edb473186f2.title_ko: 영상 생성 '클링 4.0' 및 감정 조절 음성 '드라마 3' 등 신규 AI 모델 6종 출시
ee85afdfd4a43edb473186f2.summary_ko: 클링 AI의 영상 생성 모델 '클링 4.0', 감정 조절이 가능한 피시 오디오의 '드라마 3' 등 다양한 신규 인공지능 모델과 도구들이 대거 공개되었다. 스마트폰 구동 소형 모델부터 실시간 게임 생성 및 로봇 조작 모델까지 전반적인 AI 기술 발전이 이뤄지고 있다.

b39fb3c87584d4df6e86625f.title_ko: 5대 은행장, 금융권 해킹 사고 관련 정무위 국감 출석
b39fb3c87584d4df6e86625f.summary_ko: 금융권 연쇄 해킹 사고와 관련해 5대 시중은행장이 국회 정무위원회 국정감사에 증인으로 출석한다. 이번 국감에서는 AI를 활용한 해킹으로 인한 개인정보 유출 경위와 보안 투자, 경영진의 관리 책임 등에 대한 질의가 집중될 예정이다.

f7d7903b3c793e04ef5e0ed0.title_ko: 구글, 양자컴퓨터 오류 정정 기술로 오류율 대폭 낮춰
f7d7903b3c793e04ef5e0ed0.summary_ko: 구글 퀀텀 AI 연구진이 양자 프로세서 윌로우에서 매직 스테이트 배양 기술을 구현해 핵심 계산 오류를 크게 줄였다. 대규모 양자컴퓨터 구현을 위한 하드웨어 부담을 덜어줄 실용화의 발판을 마련했다.

curation.reason_ko: 구글이 양자컴퓨터의 핵심 오류를 대폭 줄이는 새로운 오류 정정 기술을 구현했습니다.

6012a3d5f7f43ba4493848a1.title_ko: 정부, 휴머노이드 로봇 확산 대응 안전 가이드라인 마련 착수
6012a3d5f7f43ba4493848a1.summary_ko: 정부의 휴머노이드 로봇 시범 보급 확대 계획에 맞춰 한국로봇산업진흥원 등이 안전성과 성능을 평가하기 위한 가이드라인과 검증 기준 마련에 착수했다. 기존 산업용 로봇과 다른 전신 이동 및 AI 오판 가능성 등을 고려한 전용 기준 제정이 추진된다.

3af5054225626a04d8e2f212.title_ko: 2026년 API 보안 리포트: 정상 요청 위장한 API 공격 급증
3af5054225626a04d8e2f212.summary_ko: 최근 기업들을 겨냥한 대규모 데이터 유출 사고의 상당수가 권한 검증이 부실한 API를 악용한 것으로 나타났다. 공격자는 정상적인 요청과 인증정보를 사용해 시그니처 기반의 기존 웹방화벽을 우회하고 있어, 가시성 확보와 전용 API 보안 솔루션 도입의 필요성이 커지고 있다.

2ad235e5d6dec0d50810432c.title_ko: 지속가능 보안: 통제 중심을 넘어선 인간중심 보안과 정의
2ad235e5d6dec0d50810432c.summary_ko: 현대 기업의 과도한 보안 통제와 복잡한 인증 절차가 구성원들에게 피로감을 주는 역설을 짚어본다. 존 롤스와 마이클 샌델의 철학을 바탕으로 약자를 배려하는 공정한 아키텍처 설계와 연대에 기반한 신뢰 문화 구축의 중요성을 강조한다.

b62b2077e18f6f494bf69dec.title_ko: 오픈AI 녹음 장치 설치 혐의 전직 직원, 도주 목적 부인하며 보석 신청
b62b2077e18f6f494bf69dec.summary_ko: 오픈AI 사무실에 몰래 녹음 장치를 설치한 혐의로 체포된 전직 직원이 사우디아라비아행 편도 항공권은 도주 목적이 아니며 평소 여행 방식이었다고 주장하며 보석을 신청했다. 법원은 구금 여부를 결정할 심리를 진행할 예정이다.

014f716578014a25b7eda016.summary_ko: 행정안전부가 총사업비 2857억 원 규모의 차세대 지방행정공통시스템(시도새올) 구축 사업에서 상용 소프트웨어를 분리발주하기로 결정했다. 최대 800억 원대로 추정되는 상용 소프트웨어를 별도 발주함으로써 국산 소프트웨어 기업의 참여 기회를 넓히고 제값 받기를 유도한다는 취지다. 다만 제품 간 호환성과 책임 소재 조율 등이 과제로 꼽힌다.

3731c16da05d9f97037767ae.title_ko: 삼성디스플레이·LG디스플레이, 내년 대규모 디스플레이 투자 논의 착수
3731c16da05d9f97037767ae.summary_ko: 한국 디스플레이 업계가 내년 대규모 설비 투자를 위한 논의에 착수했다. 삼성디스플레이는 아산 2단지(A7 공장) 설비 투자를 추진하며, LG디스플레이는 파인메탈마스크가 없는 적녹청 유기발광다이오드 '플립' 전용 라인 구축을 검토 중이다. 양사의 투자는 국내 소재·부품·장비 업계에도 긍정적인 기회가 될 것으로 전망된다.

49ba72c8292a6833c48fe9f4.title_ko: 정부·민간 공동 투자로 국방용 반도체 자립화 추진…투자형 R&D 시동

CVE-2026-102503.description: Missing Authentication for Critical Function (CWE-306) and Missing Authorization (CWE-862) in the /libp2p-http ingress server (StartIngressServer in cmd/sam-node/node.go) in Google OSS Agent Mesh (SAM) versions 0.1.0-alpha.1 through 0.1.0-alpha.2 allow an unauthenticated remote libp2p peer to bypass Biscuit capability policy enforcement and invoke arbitrary registered backend services (including command/stdio-backed MCP servers, A2A, and inference endpoints). While the MCP protocol stream handler enforces WithBiscuitAuth and Authorize checks, the parallel /libp2p-http ingress routes requests directly to backend service handlers without verifying a Biscuit token or mesh enrollment. Users should upgrade to version 0.1.0-alpha.3 or later.
CVE-2026-102503.summary_ko: Google OSS Agent Mesh(SAM)의 libp2p-http 인그레스 서버에서 인증 및 권한 부여가 누락되어, 인증되지 않은 원격 피어가 Biscuit 정책을 우회하고 임의의 백엔드 서비스를 호출할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: 구글 OSS Agent Mesh에서 인증 우회로 임의 서비스 호출이 가능한 치명적 취약점입니다.

CVE-2026-111441.description: 在 openGauss-server 的 src/gausskernel/cbb/utils/hll/hll.cpp 中，内置函数 HllObjectUnpack() 存在长度校验缺陷。该函数从用户提供的 packed HLL 解析 lenUsed 与 lenTotal 后，仅检查输入长度足以覆盖 HLL_HEAD_SIZE + lenUsed，随后按 lenTotal 分配缓冲区、按 lenUsed 调用 memcpy_s() 拷贝输入，既未校验 lenTotal >= lenUsed，也将 memcpy_s() 目标大小写成 lenUsed 而非实际分配的 lenTotal，导致安全拷贝无法拦截越界写。hll_in()、hll_print()、hll_cardinality() 等 SQL 入口会走同一解包路径。因此，普通数据库连接用户只需构造 lenTotal 小于 lenUsed 的畸形 packed HLL（例如经 ::hll 进入 hll_in()），即可触发服务端堆越界写，存在内存破坏风险。此问题随 packed HLL 解包函数 HllObjectUnpack() 进入代码，v2.1.0 起即存在。受影响版本包括 2.1.0、3.0.x、3.1.x、5.0.x、5.1.0、6.0.x，以及 7.0.0-RC1、7.0.0-RC2、7.0.0-RC3。该问题已在 7.0.0-LTS 版本修复，通过在 HllObjectUnpack() 中补齐 lenUsed <= lenTotal 校验，并将 memcpy_s() 的目标大小改为实际分配的 lenTotal。修复 PR 见 https://gitcode.com/opengauss/openGauss-server/pull/9380 。
CVE-2026-111441.summary_ko: openGauss-server의 HllObjectUnpack() 함수에서 길이 검증 결함으로 인해, 사용자가 조작한 packed HLL 입력을 통해 서버단에서 힙 영역의 메모리 파괴 및 오버플로우가 발생할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: openGauss-server의 HllObjectUnpack 함수에서 힙 이뤄지기 및 메모리 파괴 취약점이 존재합니다.

CVE-2026-16487.description: A flaw was found in bootc when operating with the default containers signature policy. Automatic or manual upgrades of a mutable image tag may apply unsigned content for registries that fall through to insecureAcceptAnything, allowing an attacker who can update that tag to execute arbitrary OS content as the host root filesystem on reboot.

CVE-2026-104627.description: The Gitea OpenID association callback in the security settings accepted a positive OpenID 2.0 assertion without checking that the signed-in user had started the linking. Because OpenID 2.0 allows unsolicited assertions, an attacker-controlled OpenID provider could attach the attacker's identity to the account of a signed-in victim who opened a crafted link, and the attacker could then sign in as the victim through OpenID login, which does not apply the local TOTP or WebAuthn checks. The callback now requires a time-limited `state` value bound to the user.
CVE-2026-104627.summary_ko: Gitea의 OpenID 연동 콜백이 로그인된 사용자의 연동 시작 여부를 확인하지 않고 OpenID 2.0 어설션을 수락합니다. 이로 인해 공격자는 조작된 링크를 통해 피해자의 계정에 자신의 신원을 연결하고 피해자로 로그인할 수 있습니다.

curation.reason_ko: Gitea의 OpenID 연동 콜백 검증 누락으로 공격자가 피해자 계정으로 로그인할 수 있습니다.

83adae590270545156d6ce2a.title_original: Recoverability-Controlled Safety Miscalibration in Large Language Models
83adae590270545156d6ce2a.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Safety-aligned language models are expected to refuse harmful requests while remaining useful for benign ones. However, because many evaluations score only the final response, they often conflate intent understanding with response-level safety behavior. To address this, we introduce RiskCueBench, a recoverability-controlled benchmark that separates these two stages by first measuring whether a model can successfully recover a high-level intent and then evaluating its safety behavior on the same prompt. RiskCueBench contains 160 latent intents and 640 abstract non-operational surface prompts across eight risk categories. The benchmark covers 25 completed model groups and 32,000 successful model outputs with final rubric-adjudicated labels. When conditioning on pairs where both surface forms are recoverable, we find that increased contextualized specificity induces a shift toward less safe behavior. Specifically, paired bootstrap estimates show that the refusal rate and global safety score decrease by 0.175 and 0.440, respectively. Furthermore, mixed effects modeling corroborates a 0.107 increase in unsafe cooperation. These results show that the safety behavior can be miscalibrated to the surface form even after the intent has been recovered, motivating safety evaluations that report response behavior conditional on semantic recoverability.

ed10dc7b3ac6a532a7f55118.title_original: An Agentic ENF Framework for Forensic Video Authentication Against Generative AI
ed10dc7b3ac6a532a7f55118.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22440v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Generative models now synthesise video that is hard to distinguish from genuine footage, and learned detectors that key on a generator's artefacts degrade sharply on unseen models. This paper develops a forensic framework that authenticates video by a signal that generation does not control: the electric network frequency (ENF), the mains-driven hum in audio and flicker in video. A unified two-channel detector extracts the ENF from audio and from rolling-shutter video through one second harmonic estimator and a shared network; a synthetic-injection training method, driven by an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck drift model and anchored to real recordings, overcomes the scarcity of labelled ENF data; a reference-matching channel verifies a claimed time of recording and recovers an unknown one; and a two-axis agentic orchestrator fuses recording authenticity with content-manipulation evidence under an asymmetric rule, escalating expensive detectors only when needed. A central finding reframes the task: an ENF-band flicker is present in generated video at a prominence indistinguishable from real footage, so its presence is not proof of authenticity, and authentication must rest on consistency with an independent reference rather than on presence. c8774bc22c1f9c0c42ca70f2.title_original: Capital Costs Protect the Network: Mining Gap Dynamics in Proof-of-Work Blockchains Under a Stochastic Mempool
c8774bc22c1f9c0c42ca70f2.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22451v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Proof-of-Work blockchains increasingly rely on transaction fees to keep miners engaged as block subsidies decline. An immediate outcome of this is that miners may sit idle at the start of a round until enough high-fee transactions accumulate in order to make mining worthwhile. This idle period is known as the mining gap. We model the high-fee transaction backlog as a Lindley-type recursion under a two-tier fee market and use its stationary distribution to characterize the mining gap. Under Bitcoin's difficulty-adjustment mechanism, the expected gap grows strictly with the hashpower active on the network and consumes the entire round as that hashpower grows without bound. A free-entry condition determines a unique long-run equilibrium hashpower. Capital cost caps the equilibrium hashpower and prevents the mining gap from occupying the entire round. We further characterize how the block subsidy, transaction fees, and operating cost shape the equilibrium hashpower and the mining gap.

5df14ccd5acfe0b4117f81c6.title_original: Erase the Mark, Preserve the Motion: Temporally Consistent Removal of Video Watermarks
5df14ccd5acfe0b4117f81c6.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recent advances in video generation have increased the demand for reliable watermarking for copyright protection, yet the robustness of video watermarks against removal attacks remains underexplored. Most watermark-removal methods originate from the image domain: signal optimization injects imperceptible pixel-domain perturbations, whereas generative resynthesis produces a visually similar instance through diffusion synthesis. When extended to videos, the former introduces temporally varying noise that causes visible flickering, while the latter regenerates fine-grained structures inconsistently across frames, leading to structural motion inconsistency. To evaluate video watermark robustness, we propose PoseRegen, a pose-consistent reconstruction framework that removes watermarks while preserving the original content and motion. PoseRegen first applies a temporally shared viewpoint transformation to disrupt watermark-bearing spatial patterns and then jointly reconstructs the transformed sequence with a pose-conditioned video model. A frozen video DiT processes the complete sequence with its reference-video latent, and full-sequence Flow Matching supervision keeps identity and background consistent across frames. To further preserve motion structure, we introduce a lightweight Pose-Conditioned Motion Consistency Adapter that adapts the frozen backbone to temporally ordered pose guidance and constrains body-part trajectories throu

bc2f851673f1b41a559c1289.title_original: Everyone's a little bit racist: a novel ML backdoor attack in black-box mode
bc2f851673f1b41a559c1289.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22459v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Backdoors are among the most impactful attacks against Machine Learning (ML), yet most existing methods assume some form of training-time poisoning or direct model manipulation. This is often considered sufficient to assume that existing systems are not exposed to actual risks. In this paper, we introduce Backdoor-as-a-Service, a model-agnostic, fully black-box technique that, instead of installing a backdoor, activates it in the form of a latent secondary task leveraging on an already present behavior. Our tool uses genetic search to discover input transformations that induce systematic output differences aligned with an attacker-defined task, without modifying training data, architecture, or weights. We verify our approach against two targets. First, we target a MNIST digits classifier that we coerce into implementing a binary letter-recognition task. Then, we attack a production-grade NSFW classifier using face-specific perturbations to turn it into a proxy for demographic-group classification. In both cases, our method successfully enables the target backdoor. Finally, we discuss the existing countermeasures to assess the actual risk for the deployed systems.

6553434c4a309eb735e7b0b5.title_original: Model-as-a-Trojan: Self-Activating Covert DNS Exfiltration Baked Into the Weights of an LLM Agent
6553434c4a309eb735e7b0b5.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22578v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Open-weight models are downloaded from public hubs and run inside agent harnesses that grant them tools, most powerfully, a shell, under the assumption that a sandbox contains whatever the model might do. This paper demonstrates that the assumption has a blind spot: the weights themselves can be the malware, and the sandbox's last open door, DNS, is enough. We fine-tune an open-weight LLM so that a single covert behavior lives in its parameters: on the first turn of every conversation, whenever the model infers from its context that a shell tool is available, it emits one self-contained command that reads a secret from the runtime environment, base32-encodes it, chunks it, and exfiltrates it as DNS queries toward an attacker-controlled authoritative name server. It then answers the user normally and never mentions, or repeats, the act. Because the channel is DNS, the attack completes from inside a container with no internet egress beyond name resolution - measured payload-level and model-level behind an egress firewall that drops every non-DNS packet, with the secret reconstructed from the gateway resolver's query log. c090cf4d71032b31fb07e80e.title_original: Can SOLARBURST go silicon? A systematic analysis on software supply chain attacks for VLSI design flows
c090cf4d71032b31fb07e80e.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22580v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An attacker targeting the software supply chain (SWSC) of VLSI tools can fully subvert the VLSI design pipeline through purely software level compromises. However, cur- rent literature on both SWSC and VLSI hardware security has not explored how software can be used to subvert the security of the VLSI design flow. In order to bridge this gap, this paper presents a systematic analysis of the vulnerable surface of VLSI from a SWSC standpoint. We carry this anal- ysis through three major activities. First, we did an empirical analysis of VLSI software suites, focusing on their software composition, security features, and tool interactions within the VLSI design flow. Second, we develop a VLSI-SWSC attack taxonomy model that links software supply chain at- tacks and their mechanisms to the VLSI attacks they enable, the design-flow stages they affect, and their resulting security outcomes, allowing us to identify 717 possible new attacks, including 60 high feasibility attacks supported by evidence collected in our empirical analysis. Third, we identify what possible security outcomes can be achieved by an attacker from these attacks and produce a comprehensive VLSI SWSC threat model. We evaluate the feasibility of the attacks identi- fied by our taxonomy across VLSI design stages and assess existing defenses to determine which attacks are mitigated and which remain unaddressed. 0fada5eefe2224e50438dd30.title_original: StratFL: Countering Covert Model Poisoning Attacks with Strategic Federated Learning
0fada5eefe2224e50438dd30.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22626v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Advanced persistent threats (APTs) are a major concern in federated learning (FL) deployments in critical sectors such as healthcare, and finance. Traditional defense mechanisms fail to contain APTs due to their intermittent attacking behavior. This paper addresses a specific type of APT called covert model poisoning (CMP) where the attacker intermittently injects poisoned model updates in a covert manner. The interaction between the FL server and a CMP attacker is modeled as an imperfect repeated game where both players cannot observe each other's actions. A novel adversarial search algorithm called StratFL is designed alongside novel belief update algorithms at both the server and adversary. Experiments are designed using MNIST and CIFAR-10 datasets to evaluate and compare StratFL's performance against state-of-the-art methods. Empirical convergence of belief update algorithms is demonstrated across various security vignettes. At the same time, StratFL is found to exhibit an improved accuracy of 10% compared to state-of-the-art methods.

4b47800c1d458a4aa41788b4.title_original: Exploring The Empirical Privacy Landscape of Synthetic Data
4b47800c1d458a4aa41788b4.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22659v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Methods for training language models on sensitive data differ in how they balance capability gains against the risk of leaking private information. In this paper, we present a controlled comparison of data-level and training-level interventions for navigating the capability-privacy tradeoff on synthetic medical records with canaries to probe for leakage. Direct finetuning performs best on capability metrics but leads to the most privacy leakage, while DP-SGD reduces leakage at substantial cost to capabilities. Generating synthetic data from these records offers a more favorable balance, particularly when guided by a uniqueness-aware instruction to replace private details. Relative to naive paraphrasing, privacy-aware rewriting improves privacy protection across a variety of different rewriting models. We also find that more capable rewriting models generally reduce the risks of downstream privacy leakage, although held-out fit does not improve monotonically and increased test-time compute yields inconsistent gains. Overall, these results highlight privacy-aware rewriting as a promising direction for achieving a more favorable trade-off between capabilities and empirical privacy compared to other training-level methods, and our evaluation framework supports comparisons of future models and methods.

3f05ba49917f6b9f5b73bd03.title_original: What It Is, Not What It Says: Securing Agentic Browsing Interactions with Web Semantics
3f05ba49917f6b9f5b73bd03.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AI agents increasingly browse the web on users' behalf, yet they consume webpages as screenshots or text, exposing their LLMs to unvetted third-party content. Browsers enforce semantics under which what an element can do depends on what it is and where it comes from, not on what it says. Agents flatten these semantics, so injected text can persuade the LLM to exercise the user's authority for content that has none. As LLMs remain easy to persuade, the agent's interface to the web must itself ensure the integrity of what the agent reads, interprets, and does. We propose Intact, which runs on an unmodified browser. Intact builds GenTree, a bespoke representation that captures provenance and web semantics. Intact passes the page via GenTree to the LLM one element at a time, so the LLM decides on each element without any other element's text. Its harness executes each step only within the capabilities of the step's element and asks the user before acting on third-party content. On 1,270 real webpages, GenTree attributes 2.3x as many elements to third parties as the browser, which misattributes 58.7% of them to the first party. On 1,091 of these webpages with injected attacks, only 12.8% of attacks get through Intact's planner, each at most as a consent request, against 73.1% for a conventional planner. Isolation disrupts functionality on only 3.7% of tasks, and a parallel schedule could remove most of its added latency.

34a7ddf75cbf1597ff36cb90.title_original: ACE: An AI-Orchestrated Intrusion Detection and Compliance Mapping Engine
34a7ddf75cbf1597ff36cb90.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22702v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study proposes the Automated Compliance Engine (ACE), an AI-orchestrated framework that links intrusion detection, regulatory control mapping, and automated countermeasure deployment for security operations environments. ACE integrates Suricata IDS, a LangGraph five-stage workflow, retrieval-augmented generation, NIST SP 800-53 Rev. 5 control retrieval, large language model-based control ranking, and SSH-based Suricata rule deployment. The framework was evaluated in a two-virtual-machine laboratory using eight simulated attack scenarios and three legitimate traffic tests. ACE processed all eight attack alerts, achieved 100% alert detection, 0% false positives across legitimate traffic tests, generated deployable AUTO rules for 37.5% of alerts, verified 100% deployment of generated rules, and achieved an average NIST control-mapping confidence score of 0.87. The DeepEval assessment produced 1.0 scores for answer relevancy and faithfulness, while the hallucination score reflected known LLM-as-judge calibration limitations. The evaluation was conducted in a controlled environment with a limited attack set. Further validation is required using enterprise-scale telemetry, multiple IDS sensors, and an analyst-in-the-loop review. The results demonstrate how AI-assisted security automation can reduce analyst effort in translating IDS alerts into compliance-relevant evidence and defensive actions. c75a081d560bc710f6d200ad.title_original: The LLM-Attacker: A Unified Red-Team Framework for Privacy Evaluation of Split and Distributed LLM Systems
c75a081d560bc710f6d200ad.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22722v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Split language models keep input text on a client but send intermediate representations to a server. Attacks can reconstruct text from these messages. Comparing privacy evaluations is difficult when attackers see different messages, know different model weights or use different datasets and recovery measures. We present LLM-Attacker, a framework that records these choices and lets researchers check, compare and extend an evaluation. Compatible attacks reuse recorded messages, and their predictions are saved for independent scoring. The scoring rule requires a linked undefended reference before a defence can pass. Reports also identify attacks that remain untested. In a controlled GPT-2 experiment, adding gradients returned during training increased token recovery from 94.20% to 97.38% and exact-document recovery from 13.71% to 37.77%. The 95% interval for the token gain lay above the two-percentage-point threshold fixed before testing. This experiment is shared with a companion study; here, it tests how the evaluation responds to a change in attacker access. Further studies measure how corpus choice and compression defences affect recovery, compare an adapted published attack with its reference implementation, and test the measurement code. edd43462e52c2360ca439f63.title_original: Veil-Then-Reveal: Protecting PII Privacy via Reversible Pseudo-Anonymization in Zero-Trust User--LLM Interaction
edd43462e52c2360ca439f63.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22800v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly process sensitive documents and personal information, yet sending prompts containing personally identifiable information (PII) to remote providers exposes data subjects and organizations to risks from logging, retention, model training, and unintended disclosure. Existing anonymization methods often mask or remove PII, while conventional encryption eliminates the lexical and structural cues needed for effective LLM processing. We present Veil-then-Reveal (VtR), a user-side PII pseudo-anonymization framework for privacy-preserving LLM interaction under a zero-trust threat model. VtR treats remote LLM providers as untrusted and sends only pseudo-anonymized prompts, keeping plaintext PII on the user. VtR first detects PII and replaces it with realistic, same-type, in-vocabulary surrogates before prompts leave the user's device, preserving their linguistic and structural properties. It combines format-preserving encryption (FPE) for structured PII, such as phone and credit-card numbers, with a keyed-hash dictionary and secure vault for semantic PII, such as names, locations, and organizations. Session-specific mappings provide cross-session unlinkability, while user-side restoration reversibly replaces surrogates with their original values in LLM responses. 77e62efa6b908594475299b8.title_original: GRAD: Graph-Structured Antibody Defense for LLM Agents
77e62efa6b908594475299b8.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22828v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Memory poisoning and decomposition attacks distribute malicious evidence across the operations of large language model agents. Existing request-level defenses can miss such attacks because they assess individual inputs without connecting earlier information to later actions. Moreover, detectors must adapt as task contexts change, while updates to shared parameters can impair previously learned detection capabilities. To address these challenges, we propose GRAD, which combines graph-based evidence aggregation across operations with an extensible collection of detection experts. Its Semantic-Structural Understanding Module (SSUM) jointly encodes operation text, event attributes, and typed candidate relations in an execution graph to aggregate distributed attack evidence into a graph-level risk score. Its Continual Antibody Adaptation (CAA) adds experts on frozen encoder snapshots and routes inputs by observable graph signatures, acquiring and reusing detection capabilities as tasks arrive. Across Decomp, MCP, and MRT, GRAD achieves AUROCs of 97.19%, 77.59%, and 86.60%, respectively, outperforming Sequential Monitor and locally adapted Agent-Sentry and NeuroTaint. CAA improves final accuracy by 13.08 percentage points over Replay on the cross-dataset task stream. The gain remains 9.05 points with equal family/base-case weights within each task. Its compact drop-in gate performs local model inference in milliseconds without monitor

3627f00be3a7cc20850ccb40.title_original: Stealthy Poisoning Attacks via Reused KV Cache of Reasoning
3627f00be3a7cc20850ccb40.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22873v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Modern large language model (LLM) systems reuse key-value (KV) caches to accelerate inference. Recent work has shown that reusing KV caches from reasoning traces can also improve task performance, similar to retrieval-augmented generation (RAG). We demonstrate that this form of KV cache reuse introduces new poisoning vulnerabilities. We propose R$^2$ECAP (Reused Reasoning-Cache Poisoning), a black-box attack that plants poisoned reasoning traces solely through interactions with a system's chat interface. R$^2$ECAP constructs two traces: a preceding trace that steers the model toward an adversarial target and a retained trace that carries this target. Because the retained trace is generated conditioned on the preceding trace, its KV cache preserves residual adversarial influence, even after the preceding trace and its cache entries are discarded. We evaluate R$^2$ECAP on three open-weight LLMs and three datasets. R$^2$ECAP achieves up to 79% attack success rate (ASR) and outperforms HijackKV, a state-of-the-art white-box KV poisoning attack, in 8 of 9 resource-constrained settings. It also achieves 46% ASR in a realistic reasoning-trace retrieval system. Finally, R$^2$ECAP remains stealthy, with only 1% of its retained responses detected by a popular prompt injection detector.

3e16de454c92ea0f0392befb.title_original: RAMP: Toward Ubiquitous Quantum-Safe Key Distribution as a Service
3e16de454c92ea0f0392befb.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22879v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) offers a security foundation independent of computational hardness assumptions. However, its reliance on specialized hardware limits access by ordinary users. Turning QKD into a service poses a fundamental trust challenge, as the providers that supply QKD-derived material themselves could retain knowledge of the keying inputs of users. This makes end-to-end confidentiality solely depend on the trustworthiness of the service infrastructure. We present RAMP, a service-oriented framework that decouples QKD material generation from key consumption. Providers operate QKD infrastructure and supply raw-key materials, while users securely acquire, mask, and locally process them into final keys without operating QKD devices. RAMP employs reconciliation-preserving masking compatible with both DV- and CV-QKD. It mitigates the trust dependence by separating the QKD-service and user-side masking domains. We formalize complementary confidentiality guarantees: RAMP protects the final key even if colluding providers expose their complete raw-key views, provided the masking domain remains secure; conversely, exposing the complete masking state does not break final-key secrecy as long as the QKD source and acquisition paths remain protected. The results establish the dual-domain security boundary of RAMP. We implement RAMP using experimentally acquired QKD data and standardized quantum-safe cryptography. After acqui

82e1cc5e704d0735dc67beba.title_original: Provable Authority: A Protocol for Verifiable Authority Resolution and Control Across Human, Organizational, and Agentic Transactions
82e1cc5e704d0735dc67beba.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22899v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Payment systems authenticate users, devices, accounts, and cryptographic credentials, but a relying party, such as a counterparty, payment rail, marketplace, or autonomous agent runtime, generally cannot obtain compact, independently verifiable evidence that the party presenting one exact transaction holds current organizational authority to execute it under the applicable evidence, policy, budget, and approval state. Agentic commerce makes this gap operationally urgent: a software agent can produce a valid signature while acting outside its delegated purpose, after its sponsor's authority has changed, or on transaction details that differ from those a human approved. We describe the ChainIT Authority Protocol, a subject-neutral and rail-neutral pre-execution authority and evidence control plane. The protocol separates durable identity, a versioned organizational authority record (the Authority Resolution Pactvera), sourced evidence assertions, deterministic reason-coded policy predicates, and organization-configured dispositions; binds each decision and human approval to a canonical transaction digest; reserves capacity atomically so that limits hold under concurrency; and authorizes commit only through a single-use, sender-constrained Execution Authorization Credential consumed at the rail adapter, with append-only lifecycle evidence sealed after the terminal outcome. 409cb565d9a02409139a54c1.title_original: Provable Compliance: A Protocol for Runtime Compliance Evidence and Transaction-Specific Decisioning
409cb565d9a02409139a54c1.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22913v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Regulated institutions already perform onboarding, screening, monitoring, and review, but compliance evidence ages, and whether it supports a decision depends on the institution, product, subject, counterparty, transaction, jurisdiction, risk tier, and purpose. A relying party therefore often cannot obtain compact, attributable proof of which evidence, policy, authority, and transaction context were current when a decision was made, a gap that grows as authority is delegated to software agents and scheduled workflows. We describe ChainIT Provable Compliance, the compliance-side layer of the ChainIT Authority Protocol. Each sourced or institution-generated fact is represented as a separate Evidence Assertion VDT with provenance, freshness, confidence, permitted purpose, and privacy classification; a versioned Compliance Policy Profile selects the applicable rules; a Business Rules Engine returns deterministic, reason-coded predicate results; and the organization's configured Workflow Engine composes them into a signed, time-bounded Compliance Decision VDT for one reliance event. The decision contributes a single predicate, Compliance Decision Permits, to session-eligibility and transaction-policy decisions. It never independently authorizes payment: only a final Allow together with an exact transaction digest, atomic capacity reservation, and a single-use execution credential can commit value. c00184166f05844489d644b7.title_original: When Core-Network Elements Become Reachable: Field-Level Exploitability Analysis in Diameter
c00184166f05844489d644b7.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22943v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The increasing exposure of cellular core-network elements to public networks has turned Diameter signaling interfaces into a practical attack surface. While large language models (LLMs) show promise for protocol exploitability analysis, we find that their judgments on Diameter can be unreliable because they may deviate from the tacit analysis discipline followed by security experts and reach conclusions without considering complete protocol evidence. To address this challenge, we present LENS, an LLM-based system for reliable field-level Diameter exploitability analysis. LENS guides LLMs using both exploitability-analysis discipline and the protocol evidence needed for analysis. It infers analysis discipline from existing exploit writeups and evidence-collection guidance from exploitability-analysis failures, enabling systematic evidence collection, exploitability assessment, and proof-of-concept (PoC) attack generation when applicable. Our experiments show that LENS performs reliable analysis across four LLMs and repeated runs, achieving mean recall of 94.00% to 98.00%, precision of 78.73% to 88.94%, and accuracy of 84.00% to 92.00%. We find that more than 25% of field paths in the S6a and Cx interfaces are exploitable under the considered threat model. We further assess their impact on practical implementations and uncover 95 previously unknown vulnerabilities, including 17 in open-source EPC/IMS implementations and 78 in comm

24cbc268a1a15a7f9ecdab6a.title_original: SAFE-Mem: Secure Agentic Memory with Fine-Grained Authority and Governance-Aware Retrieval
24cbc268a1a15a7f9ecdab6a.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22959v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents increasingly rely on persistent memory to support long-term reasoning and personalized interactions. However, information collected from external sources can introduce security risks when untrusted claims (i.e., atomic statements) are later treated as authorized preferences, policies, or permissions. Existing defenses typically rely on content-based filtering or coarse-grained provenance tracking, which either fail to prevent unauthorized memory use or block legitimate information, sacrificing memory utility. To address these limitations, we propose SAFE-Mem, a fine-grained memory governance framework that improves security while preserving legitimate memory use. First, SAFE-Mem annotates each claim with three governance labels (i.e., kind, authority, and scope) to capture its provenance and permitted use. Second, governance-aware retrieval matches query requirements with claim permissions to block unauthorized influence while retaining legitimate information. Third, a governance-enabled memory graph connects source sentences, claims, and entities to support provenance tracking and efficient retrieval. Across four LLM backbones on MPBench and LoCoMo, SAFE-Mem attains the lowest attack success among defenses that retain legitimate memory, at least 77% below the strongest of them, and the highest answer accuracy of all evaluated defenses, improving it by up to 15%. The code is available at https:/

4bf95ae0dd919cae945d7f1d.title_original: Surprise Masking: Private Data Filtering with Model Likelihoods
4bf95ae0dd919cae945d7f1d.excerpt: arXiv:2610.22988v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Data useful for language model (LM) training can contain private or unwanted information that is at risk of being learned or memorized. We propose Surprise Masking (SM), a simple form of perplexity filtering that uses a publicly available reference model to identify unwanted spans and suppress learning from them while preserving the rest of each example. On synthetic code benchmarks, we show SM improves the privacy-utility tradeoff over standard masking methods and PII filtering. In fine-tuning experiments, SM reduces approximate extraction of private values from revealed prefixes from 66.3% to 2.3% and the reproduction of stylistic coding quirks from 23.6% to 1.3%, both while preserving performance on the evaluated coding tasks. We also evaluate SM for sanitizing datasets by directly removing unwanted content. Here, SM outperforms DePA, a perplexity-based defense for detecting poisoned dead code, while specialized detectors perform better on broader credential and PII benchmarks. Across eleven settings, we find that SM's downstream success is predictable from the separation of unwanted and useful content in the distribution, and it is particularly useful with code data. Ultimately, SM is an inexpensive, adaptable method to preserve valuable examples while reducing the learning of unwanted information.

4b6f9b364ed98518b0b45852.title_original: ECHO: Replacing the Compliance Proxy with Response Harmfulness in Optimization-Based Jailbreak Attack
4b6f9b364ed98518b0b45852.excerpt: arXiv:2610.23030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Despite extensive safety alignment, large language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks. Existing optimization-based attacks share a single objective: maximize a token-level proxy of victim compliance---such as the likelihood of an affirmative prefix---computed on the prompt rather than the decoded reply. This proxy cannot distinguish a cautious hedge from a fully actionable harmful answer, leaving the search blind to what the model actually says. We propose ECHO (Evaluation-Conditioned Harmfulness Optimization), which replaces the compliance proxy with response-level, continuous harmfulness scores from HarmSig, a 1.7B regressor grounded in actual harmful capability. ECHO couples HarmSig with five word-level perturbation operators and Keyword-Anchored Beam Search with global top-m memory, under a strict black-box threat model. Across five open-weight victims on AdvBench, ECHO achieves up to 0.898 StrongREJECT mean score and 89.23% HarmBench success. Our code is publicly available at https://github.com/STANWYW/echo.

e5421fedf245ae18e4b132ed.title_original: Aspire: Practical Batch Queries on Dynamic Encrypted Database with Full Leakage Suppression
e5421fedf245ae18e4b132ed.excerpt: arXiv:2610.23057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Leakage-abuse attacks against encrypted database systems exploit semantic leakage and pose a severe threat to the confidentiality of plaintext data and queries. To address this problem, we propose a zero-leakage encrypted database that rules out leakage-abuse attacks, which fundamentally rely on semantic leakage. We first distinguish between two kinds of zero-leakage security. Ideal zero-leakage forbids the disclosure of any information beyond public parameters, whereas restricted zero-leakage additionally permits the leakage of metadata (such as database size and query timing). We show that restricted zero-leakage is sufficient to thwart leakage-abuse attacks and is achievable in practice. We then formally define adaptive restricted zero-leakage security and present Aspire, an encrypted database that satisfies this notion. Aspire integrates probabilistic batch code and minimal perfect hashing to support efficient batch keyword queries and dynamic updates while revealing only non-semantic metadata. Experimental results demonstrate the practicality and efficiency of Aspire, showing that Aspire can achieve an amortized query latency of less than 1.38 ms (7.53 s for a batch of 5461 keyword queries), with an amortized communication cost of approximately 2.95 KB (16.1 MB in total), on a $2^{22}$ key-value pairs database.

04f911432c86907fdb895c4e.title_original: When Approval Becomes Execution: Authorization-Grounded Workflow Attacks on Tool-Using Agents
04f911432c86907fdb895c4e.excerpt: arXiv:2610.23077v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Tool-using language-model agents increasingly rely on local services for document access, approval management, and enterprise workflow execution. This paper studies an authorization-grounded workflow attack in the OpenClaw Agent Security Attack Competition, a controlled benchmark derived from SeClaw-style security task synthesis. Rather than using explicit policy-override instructions, the attack guides the agent through a locally coherent approval workflow: a protected document request is denied, the agent requests a normal approval token from the local approval service, and the returned token is supplied to the document service through authorized_by. Official submission traces show this pattern succeeding on three Enterprise OA document targets. We also conducted 23 controlled local validation experiments in the official OpenClaw execution environment: the original configuration reached the approval-token transition in 9/9 reruns and completed the exact target operation in 8/9 reruns, while single-component variants remained successful on the three document targets. The results provide concrete case evidence of an authorization-context gap: token possession can be treated as sufficient authorization even when requester identity, approver authority, resource scope, action type, destination or recipient, and business purpose are not jointly enforced.
